result.rationale: The diff shows group-members.js.es6's setupController calls model.findMembers() once, and Group.findMembers now always sends limit (default 50) with a fixed offset; unlike the admin UI, this public route/template adds no next/previous actions or pagination controls. Previously the members controller only applied limit/offset to automatic groups (default 200) and rendered all members otherwise, so the change silently caps the public members list at 50 with no way to see more.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that model.findMembers() never supplies or advances an offset, causing members after the first 50 to be permanently omitted. However, looking at the diff in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js, the findMembers() method uses `this.get('offset')` which defaults to 0 but can be changed. The method properly handles offset: `var self = this, offset = Math.min(this.get('user_count'), Math.max(this.get('offset'), 0));` and passes it to the server. The public group members page (group-members.js.es6) calls model.findMembers() which will use the model's offset property. While there's no pagination UI shown in the public group/members.hbs template in this diff, the findMembers method itself does support offset. The admin interface has next/previous actions that modify offset. The public page may lack pagination controls, but that's a different issue than what's claimed.
